mainEntity.name: Why is circumference divided by diameter always π?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every circle is a scaled copy of every other. Scaling multiplies the circumference and the diameter by the same factor, so their ratio never changes. That constant ratio is π.

mainEntity.name: How do I find the radius from the area or circumference?

acceptedAnswer.text: From the area, r = √(A ÷ π). From the circumference, r = C ÷ 2π. This calculator does both: choose what you know in the first tab.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a sector and a segment?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sector is a “pie slice” bounded by two radii and an arc. A segment is the region between an arc and its chord. The segment area is the sector area minus the triangle formed by the two radii and the chord.

mainEntity.name: How do I find a segment’s area without knowing the angle?

acceptedAnswer.text: From the chord c and height h, first find r = c² ÷ (8h) + h ÷ 2, then the central angle θ = 2·atan2(c ÷ 2, r − h), and use the segment formula ½r²(θ − sin θ). The Segment tab does this for you.

mainEntity.name: Should I use degrees or radians?

acceptedAnswer.text: The arc-length and sector-area formulas s = rθ and ½r²θ require radians. If your angle is in degrees, multiply by π ÷ 180 first — or just pick “deg” on the Sector tab and the calculator converts for you.
An annulus is the ring between two concentric circles of radii R (outer) and r (inner). Its area is π(R² − r²), which can also be written π(R − r)(R + r).
